notes.sections: Deliberately empty. TRNAME names the host road, not a hiking section - the pattern rejected for the NCT and PNT. The candidate for later is NPS's four named legs (Point Lookout-Leonardtown, Colton's Point-Port Tobacco, Port Tobacco-Smallwood, Smallwood-Oxon Cove), which cover only ~190 of the spine's miles. sec_mile is region-local.
notes.out_and_back: Piney Point Rd, Lighthouse Rd and Colton Point Rd are walked twice and kept on the axis, because NPS's published Point Lookout to Leonardtown mileage includes the trip out to the lighthouse and back. That tread therefore carries two mile values.
notes.side_route_mile: For route_kind "side", mile is LOCAL to the route and starts at 0 - disconnected trail has no position on the trail axis. junction_mile gives the spine mile where the route meets the trail.
notes.paddle: The Youghiogheny River paddle route (TRTYPE "Water Trail", TRUSE "Paddle|Kayak", TRSURFACE "Water") is drawn for corridor completeness but carries no mileage and no points.json entries - route_id "roadwalk", the non-hikeable sense, exactly as the PNT treats its Puget Sound ferry. It has no route_kind, because that vocabulary describes hikeable route and a paddle route is outside it.
notes.schema: points.json carries lat, lon, mile, route_id, route_type and state. id, sec_mile, region_id, region_name, section_id, section_name, route_kind, alt_of, junction_mile and junction_sec_mile are rebuilt at load by lib/hydrate-points.js.
notes.route_ids: Numeric ids are PINNED. legacy_route_id on each row records the descriptive id they replaced. route_id is a foreign key on hike_segments, so a rebuild must reuse these assignments and only append new ones.
notes.alternate_mile: alt-1 (the DC River Trail) carries its own route-local mile. It previously held a mile interpolated across spine miles 322.71-352.04, which is why map.js needed dist_mile to avoid overstating a hike fourfold.
